messages:

Subject: Hosted API - retention & geo matrix questions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this. We’re filling out a security questionnaire and need precise answers for a few items around hosted API data residency, retention, and deletion. The questions where we need clarity:

- Where are raw request/response payloads stored by default (region-level mapping)?
- Canonical retention windows (in days) for: full-fidelity request payloads, short-term KV/prefix cache, aggregated logs, audit traces, and backups/snapshots.
- What triggers a customer-initiated deletion and what is the timeline for: (a) removal from live storage, (b) removal from backup snapshots, (c) logs/audit traces redaction.
- Do backups/snapshots replicate cross-region by default? If yes, under what conditions?
- What proof/evidence can you provide on deletion (attestation letter, audit logs, deletion job run IDs)?

Attached is our questionnaire (Attachment: skyline_sqa_questionnaire.pdf). We’d appreciate a compact matrix (CSV is fine) mapping region -> retention windows + a short paragraph on deletion mechanics so our InfoSec team can sign off.

Best,
Elena Morales
Security Manager
Skyline Payments
(Attachment: skyline_sqa_questionnaire.pdf)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@skylinepayments.com>
Cc: sec-team@skylinepayments.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - retention & geo matrix questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I’ve answered below with a concise matrix summary and attached a downloadable CSV and a data-flow diagram for your architecture team. Please let me know if you want additional evidence artifacts (we can provide a one-off attestation PDF and relevant audit IDs).

Quick summary (hosted API):
- Region mapping: customer data for a hosted account is stored in the cloud region selected at account creation (example: us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). By default there is no cross-region replication unless explicit cross-region failover or DR is configured.

- Retention windows (default / typical):
  * Full-fidelity request/response payloads (per customer): 30 days.
  * Short-term KV / prefix cache (performance caches): 7 days (TTL-based, auto-evicting).
  * Aggregated service logs (ingest metrics, model call costs): 90 days raw, 365 days aggregated metrics only.
  * Audit traces (who accessed which route / model): 365 days (immutable audit trail for compliance).
  * Backups / snapshots (encrypted): 90 days for accessible snapshots; snapshot tombstones and cryptographic erasure process complete within 180 days.

- Deletion process (customer-initiated):
  1) Customer issues deletion request via Console API or Support ticket (we also accept signed deletion requests).
  2) Live data: deletion job queues immediately; most objects removed from live serving/storage within 24 hours, subject to in-flight requests.
  3) Backups/snapshots: Snapshot deletion marks the snapshot for removal; tombstones are propagated to retention controller. Actual physical/cryptographic erasure of snapshot copies finishes within 90–180 days depending on the underlying cloud provider snapshot lifecycle.
  4) Logs & audit traces: access logs required for security/forensics are retained 365 days; redaction requests can be processed but we commonly provide scoped export + redaction attestations.

- Cross-region replication: Off by default for hosted API. Cross-region replication occurs only if configured by the customer (explicit DR policy) or when account-level failover is enabled. We do not replicate customer payloads across regions for geo-compliant accounts unless requested.

- Evidence & attestations available:
  * SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) available under NDA.
  * Per-deletion run IDs and deletion job logs (we can provide a signed attestation with job run IDs and timestamps).
  * Audit logs showing the deletion request, job initiation, and final state.

Attached: redwood_geo_retention_matrix.csv (compact matrix by region) and data-flow-diagram.png.

Notes / nuance:
- For high-sensitivity PII/PCI workloads we recommend a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or Redwood Dedicated with customer-managed keys. Hosted API simplifies ops but has longer snapshot cryptographic erasure windows because of shared cloud snapshot semantics.
- Short-term caches are explicitly ephemeral and are not part of backups; they’re evicted based on TTL and LRU.

If that covers it, I’ll prepare a short deletion-attestation template we can sign. Happy to hop on a 20–30 minute call if your team wants to walk through the CSV.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Security Lead
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: redwood_geo_retention_matrix.csv, data-flow-diagram.png)

Hi Elena — following up with two operational details Mateo and I discussed internally:

- KMS & keying: Hosted accounts use per-customer envelope encryption keys managed by Redwood’s KMS integration (we call customer key material out to the cloud KMS service). For Dedicated/Private customers we can support customer-provided CMKs or HSM-backed keys to provide stronger separation.

- Snapshot lifecycle nuance: Cloud provider snapshots (block/volume snapshots) are immutable once created. Our deletion flow marks snapshots and triggers provider lifecycle policies; in practice the snapshot references are removed quickly but underlying provider retention windows mean physical copies are reclaimed within the provider SLA window (we include the provider snapshot ID in the deletion attestations).

- Logs retention exception: For legal hold or ongoing investigation we will suspend deletion for the scoped items and notify the requesting customer and our legal/compliance teams.

I’ve reviewed the CSV Mateo attached and updated a row clarifying audit-log retention and the exact fields we include in attestations (job ID, timestamp, snapshot/provider ID). If helpful I can attach a redacted example attestation.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
